dedupe_keys.name: chas cultural heritage architectural segmentation dataset

description: CHAS is a point cloud dataset of Brazilian cultural heritage buildings with ground-truth labels, made to train and test semantic segmentation for automatic building information modelling of historic structures. It was produced at the School of Technology of the State University of Campinas (UNICAMP) by Pedro Victor Vieira de Paiva, Camila Kimi Cogima, Eloisa Dezen-Kempter and Marco Antonio Garcia de Carvalho, and published on Zenodo on 26 March 2019. Coverage is five historic buildings in Brazil. Clouds come from terrestrial laser scanning and photographs taken by drone, and cover five religious and colonial buildings; each has an RGB-registered raw cloud and a labelled ground-truth cloud. Access: ten 7z archives, about 6 GB in all, openly downloadable. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: few buildings of one architectural tradition, so models trained on it transfer poorly to modern stock. Simulation uses are heritage BIM and digital twins for conservation, and as-built geometry for damage assessment of historic buildings. Related records: the BIO LoD3 point cloud benchmark.
